O.content: The chart displays blue points labeled Week 2 through Week 6 and axis titles, with no visible profit, margin, incremental-sales, control-group, or causal-method annotation.

B.text: If a broader-spend approval requires evidence that added advertising caused profitable incremental sales, then a scatterplot of weekly spend and sales without a causal design, costs, margin, or return measures is insufficient; select full-data analysis.
B.conditions: Applies if approval policy requires causal or profitability validation rather than a descriptive association.

O.content: The title reads "Weeks with Promotional Campaigns: Ad Spend vs Sales"; the horizontal axis is inscribed "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and the vertical axis is inscribed "Sales ($ thousands)".

The blue points labeled Week 2, Week 3, Week 4, Week 5, and Week 6 progress from lower-left to upper-right; each later labeled point is to the right of and higher on the page than the preceding labeled point.

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, both in $ thousands as printed, then points farther right and higher represent weeks with greater spend and greater sales. If a consistent higher-spend/higher-sales pattern across the labeled campaign weeks is sufficient evidence for a spend recommendation, select broader spend expansion.
B.conditions: Applies only if the plotted weeks are comparable campaign observations and the task permits an association-based expansion decision without requiring causal attribution, profitability, or additional controls.
